blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Geometric Series, p-Series & nth-Term Divergence Test

body.en: Geometric series converge if |r| < 1 with sum S = a / (1 - r). p-series converge if p > 1. nth-Term Test confirms divergence when limit is non-zero.

label.en: ● Precise (ε, N) Definition of Limit of a Sequence

body.en:
A sequence \(\{a_n\}\) converges to a real limit \(L\), written \(\displaystyle\lim_{n \to \infty} a_n = L\), if and only if for every \(\varepsilon > 0\), there exists an integer \(N \in \mathbb{N}\) such that:

\[ n > N \implies |a_n - L| < \varepsilon. \]

Geometric Meaning: No matter how narrow an error corridor \((L - \varepsilon, L + \varepsilon)\) is chosen around \(L\), there is a cutoff index \(N\) beyond which all subsequent terms \(a_{N+1}, a_{N+2}, \dots\) are trapped permanently inside the corridor.

Example 1: Prove using the \(\varepsilon\text{--}N\) definition that \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n} = 0\).

Proof: Let \(\varepsilon > 0\) be given. By the Archimedean Property of the real numbers, choose an integer \(N \in \mathbb{N}\) such that \(N \ge \lceil 1/\varepsilon \rceil > 0\). For any integer \(n > N\): \[ \left|\frac{1}{n} - 0\right| = \frac{1}{n} < \frac{1}{N} \le \varepsilon. \] Thus \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{1}{n} = 0\). \(\blacksquare\)

Example 2: Prove that \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{3n - 1}{2n + 5} = \frac{3}{2}\).

1. Scratchwork: We examine the error: \[ \left|\frac{3n - 1}{2n + 5} - \frac{3}{2}\right| = \left|\frac{2(3n - 1) - 3(2n + 5)}{2(2n + 5)}\right| = \left|\frac{6n - 2 - 6n - 15}{4n + 10}\right| = \frac{17}{4n + 10} < \frac{17}{4n}. \] We want \(\frac{17}{4n} < \varepsilon \iff 4n > \frac{17}{\varepsilon} \iff n > \frac{17}{4\varepsilon}\). Choose \(N = \lceil \frac{17}{4\varepsilon} \rceil\).

2. Formal Proof: Let \(\varepsilon > 0\) be arbitrary. Select \(N = \max\left(1, \left\lceil \frac{17}{4\varepsilon} \right\rceil\right)\). For any \(n > N\): \[ \left|\frac{3n - 1}{2n + 5} - \frac{3}{2}\right| = \frac{17}{4n + 10} < \frac{17}{4n} < \frac{17}{4N} \le \varepsilon. \] Hence \(\lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{3n - 1}{2n + 5} = \frac{3}{2}\). \(\blacksquare\)

body.en:
Geometric: \(S = \frac{a}{1-r}\) for \(|r| < 1\). Diverges for \(|r| \ge 1\).
p-Series: converges for \(p > 1\), diverges for \(p \le 1\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

Determine whether \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty 3\left(\frac{2}{5}\right)^n\) converges, and if so, evaluate its sum.

solution.en: This is a geometric series with ratio \(r = 2/5\). Since \(|r| = 0.4 < 1\), the series converges. First term (\(n=1\)): \(a = 3(2/5) = 6/5\). Sum: \[ S = \frac{a}{1-r} = \frac{6/5}{1 - 2/5} = \frac{6/5}{3/5} = \mathbf{2}. \]

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Determine the convergence or divergence of \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{n}{2n^3 + 5}\) using a comparison test.

solution.en: Compare to \(b_n = \frac{n}{2n^3} = \frac{1}{2n^2}\). Use the Limit Comparison Test: \[ \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{a_n}{b_n} = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{n/(2n^3+5)}{1/(2n^2)} = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac{2n^3}{2n^3+5} = 1 > 0. \] Since \(\sum \frac{1}{n^2}\) is a convergent p-series (\(p = 2 > 1\)), the series converges by LCT.

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Ratio Test & Absolute vs Conditional Convergence

body.en: Ratio Test determines absolute convergence for factorials and exponentials. Check alternating terms for conditional convergence.

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Determine whether the alternating harmonic series \(\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{n}\) converges absolutely, converges conditionally, or diverges.

solution.en: By the Alternating Series Test, \(a_n = 1/n\) is positive, decreasing, and \(\lim 1/n = 0\), so the series converges. However, the absolute value series \(\sum |a_n| = \sum 1/n\) is the harmonic series (\(p = 1\)), which diverges. Therefore, the series is conditionally convergent.
